The Harvard Classics.  1909–14.

XLIV

Above all, remember that the door stands open. Be not more fearful than children; but as they, when they weary 
of the game, cry, “I will play no more,” even so, when thou art in the like case, cry, “I will play no more,” and depart. But if thou stayest, make no lamentation.
